No, I do not believe Voat will become large enough to go that meta.

It is the cycle of social news aggregate birth/life/death. All things are intangible and impermanent. Users have certain demands and expectations of the platforms that they inhabit. As platforms fail to meet those expectations, they collapse when their users exodus. The exodus from Digg was swift and complete. I suspect reddit will hang around in some functional capacity for a much longer time - even as more and more users seek out a venue for "real" discussion. I would credit this to the sheer size of the site, and the staggering number of active niche communities covering almost any topic one could be interested in. Those small communities will act as practical sources of information and communication long after the site at large becomes a wasteland of mouthpieces and empty agendas.

In my opinion, Voat will become the next "old" reddit - but how long it maintains that status is up for debate. There are new forces at work in controlling and manipulating online discourse that did not exist at the outset of Reddit or even Digg, which died of Greed and not Malice.

At first glance, I will say it is unlikely Voat maintains the purity of its free discourse for as long as reddit did in the beginning. What safeguards there are to prevent targeted and focused disruption and manipulation of discussions are inadequate. I don't have any idea what would be adequate, but as soon as this place becomes influential enough and gets enough attention it will change for the worse... Possibly leading to a news-aggregate-whack-a-mole as users flee from one site to another in search of a place to freely exchange information and ideas.

I've been to Norway. Definitely a good country to live. The benefits are INSANE. Takes 3 months to fire someone (they HAVE to give you a warning that your performance is slipping up), government covering 80% of your pay when you are fired, a year's maternity and paternity leave, government paying for your education through-and-through (and willing to train you for a different vocation should your industry tank), healthcare being REALLY cheap (emergency room visits are free and immediate, but seeing a doctor for something minor costs $50 and has a waiting list).

Only downside is the taxes and how expensive everything is. Proportionally, their minimum wage and cost of living are a bit closer - you can afford most things making minimum wage there. But, what we make here with a decent office job is about what they make minimum wage there. But taxes past $150,000 per year or so are 40% of your income, no matter what.

Yeah, I have basically zero issues with high taxes if it means life can't shit on my head non-stop if something goes wrong. Barring that, if it helps some other poor bastard from having life shit on his head non-stop, well I'm okay with that too.
